source: Selected from the bibliography of CoT_NIAH_Counting_ICLR2027.pdf, pages 10–13.
year_convention: Conference publication year when applicable; otherwise the original publication year.

references.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
references.note: Reasoning traces improve performance on arithmetic, symbolic, and commonsense tasks.

references.title: RULER: What’s the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
references.note: Extends needle retrieval to controlled long-context tasks involving multiple records, tracing, and aggregation.

references.title: Retrieval Head Mechanistically Explains Long-Context Factuality
references.note: Identifies attention heads that retrieve information from context and tests their contribution through ablation.

references.title: Counting in Small Transformers: The Delicate Interplay between Attention and Feed-Forward Layers
references.note: Characterizes distinct counting strategies and how attention and feed-forward layers implement them in small transformers.

references.title: Not All Language Model Features Are One-Dimensionally Linear
references.note: Demonstrates circular, multidimensional features and tests their causal role, motivating analysis beyond a single linear direction.

references.title: When Models Manipulate Manifolds: The Geometry of a Counting Task
references.note: Studies curved count representations and the attention computations that construct and use them during text linebreaking.

references.title: How to Use and Interpret Activation Patching
references.note: Clarifies how prompt choice, intervention direction, and evaluation metrics affect the interpretation of patching results.

references.title: The Hydra Effect: Emergent Self-repair in Language Model Computations
references.note: Documents compensation after ablation, showing why the measured effect of removal can understate a component’s contribution.

references.title: Iteration Head: A Mechanistic Study of Chain-of-Thought
references.note: Tracks how attention mechanisms for iterative computation emerge during controlled training.

references.title: (How) Do Language Models Track State?
references.note: Identifies alternative state-tracking mechanisms in permutation tasks and relates their emergence to training and generalization.
